title: Recursive shelves: Floor ticket
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Recursively inspect half-open ranges [left,right), starting with the whole array. For each nonempty range, record its sum, then inspect its left half and right half using mid=floor((left+right)/2); stop splitting a one-element range. Produce the recorded sums in that preorder. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A shelf audit divides each occupied range in half and records its subtotal before opening smaller ranges. Mina is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

Recursively inspect half-open ranges [left,right), starting with the whole array. For each nonempty range, record its sum, then inspect its left half and right half using mid=floor((left+right)/2); stop splitting a one-element range. Produce the recorded sums in that preorder.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement recursiveShelvesFloorTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Divide-and-conquer recursion. Recursively inspect half-open ranges [left,right), starting with the whole array. For each nonempty range, record its sum, then inspect its left half and right half using mid=floor((left+right)/2); stop splitting a one-element range. Produce the recorded sums in that preorder. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with divide-and-conquer recursion. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [23,4,7,-3,19,7,12,0,12]. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives -3.
The derived sequence is [10,8,4,4,2,-2,4]. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives -2.
The derived sequence is []. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 0.
